summary: Generate 20+ English name candidates for the game, research conflicts across stores/web/trademark DBs, score and pick one

candidates.name: Echotrail
candidates.meaning: Echo + trail. Your moves leave a trail of echoes, and that trail comes after you.
candidates.rationale: 9 chars, one coined word that is easy to say (EK-oh-trail). It names the core mechanic directly: a delayed copy of your path that chases you. Built from neutral words and has no negative reading in EN/TR/DE/IT/FR/ES. Possible store title: 'Echotrail: Neon Shadow Run' (26 chars, under the 30 limit).

candidates.name: Shadowloop
candidates.meaning: Shadow + loop. Your shadow loops back through everything you just did.
candidates.rationale: 10 chars. It keeps the literal 'shadow' from the Turkish title, and 'loop' makes it clearly different from Shadow Fight-style names. Both halves are understood worldwide (loop is common in TR/DE/FR/IT/ES tech slang) and neither has a bad meaning. Fits the replay idea and the endless mode.

candidates.name: Glowtrace
candidates.meaning: Glow + trace. The traced path of a glowing character, retraced by its pursuer.
candidates.rationale: 9 chars. It fits the neon glow look (purple/teal/gold on navy) and the path-tracing mechanic. 'Trace' is the same word in French and is easy to read in the other target languages. Short, safe and works as a brand.

candidates.name: Lumbra
candidates.meaning: Coined from Latin lumen (light) + umbra (shadow): light and its shadow in one word.
candidates.rationale: 6 chars, very brandable, says the same in most languages (LOOM-bra). It sums up the game: a light character hunted by its own shadow. It also quietly echoes the 'Lumos' in the developer brand without using the Harry Potter spell itself. Spanish 'lumbre' means fire/glow, which is positive. Only minor caveat: a faint resemblance to the medical word 'lumbar', with no negative meaning in any target language.

candidates.name: Retrace
candidates.meaning: To go over the same path again, which is exactly what your shadow does.
candidates.rationale: 7 chars, a real English word that is also a French verb, so it is intuitive. It describes the mechanic exactly with no violent or dark tone. Spanish 'retraso' (delay) sounds a bit like it, which happens to fit the delay mechanic and is neutral. Pair it with a descriptor for search, e.g. 'Retrace: Escape Your Shadow' (27 chars).

candidates.name: Outpace
candidates.meaning: To move faster than something, here your own past self.
candidates.rationale: 7 chars, short and positive, and it signals reflex and speed. It avoids the famous 'OutRun' name. Italian 'pace' means peace, so there is a pleasant accidental reading and no negative meaning anywhere. Because it is generic, use it with a subtitle: 'Outpace: Dodge Your Shadow' (26 chars).

candidates.name: Echo Escape
candidates.meaning: Escape from your own echo, the delayed replay of your moves.
candidates.rationale: 11 chars. The light alliteration makes it memorable, and it states the goal (don't get caught) more plainly than any other candidate. It avoids the 'Dark Echo' pattern because it has no dark/horror wording. Simple words that players in all six languages understand.

candidates.name: Ghostrail
candidates.meaning: Ghost + trail (also reads as 'ghost rail'): the ghostly trail your past self leaves.
candidates.rationale: 9 chars. The 'ghost' idea is familiar from racing-game ghost laps that replay your previous run, which is exactly this mechanic, so arcade players get it fast. It is playful rather than scary and is fine in all target languages.

candidates.name: Neon Mimic
candidates.meaning: A neon copy that mimics every move you make.
candidates.rationale: 10 chars. It puts the visual identity (neon) and the mechanic (mimicry) together in two common words. Turkish 'mimik' (facial expression) is neutral, and 'mimic/mimique/mimica' are clear in the European languages. Friendly and fine for 13+.

candidates.name: Twinshade
candidates.meaning: Twin + shade: your shadow twin, and later two of them.
candidates.rationale: 9 chars. It nods to the stage where a second shadow joins, and 'shade' sounds more poetic than 'shadow'. Easy to say. The only near-match is German 'schade' (what a pity), which sounds different and is mild, not offensive. Clean in the other languages.

candidates.name: Glowstep
candidates.meaning: Glow + step. Every glowing step you take is copied step for step.
candidates.rationale: 8 chars, rhythmic and upbeat, suits a one-finger reflex game and the minimal geometric neon style. No negative readings in EN/TR/DE/IT/FR/ES. Works as an app icon wordmark.

candidates.name: Doppelglow
candidates.meaning: From doppelganger + glow: a glowing double that follows you.
candidates.rationale: 10 chars. 'Doppelganger' (German 'Doppel' = double) is known worldwide, so the meaning comes across right away while the coined word stays unique and playful. Pronounced DOP-el-glow. No negative meaning in any target language.

candidates.name: Umbrix
candidates.meaning: Coined from Latin umbra (shadow) + the techy '-ix' ending: a shadow-tech brand name.
candidates.rationale: 6 chars, short and distinctive, with a geometric, neon-arcade feel. Italian 'ombra' and Spanish 'umbra' make the shadow root recognisable. It is not a word in any target language, so it carries no negative meaning and is good for trademarking and app-store search, pending a name check.

candidates.name: Neon Rewind
candidates.meaning: A neon rewind of your own moves that comes back to catch you.
candidates.rationale: 11 chars. It shows the time-delay idea (your past replayed) and the neon look in two simple international words. It sounds retro-arcade, suits the 500-level / 100-map campaign, and has no negative connotations in EN/TR/DE/IT/FR/ES. Store title example: 'Neon Rewind: Shadow Escape' (26 chars).

candidates.name: Echoveer
candidates.meaning: echo + veer. Your echo (the delayed shadow) follows you, and you veer, swerving sharply to stay out of its reach.
candidates.rationale: 8 letters and easy to say in every target language (eh-ko-VEER). Dutch 'veer' means feather/spring and is positive, and none of en/tr/de/it/fr/es gives it a negative reading. The V and the double E make a sharp, geometric neon wordmark, and the V can be drawn as the diamond character. Web check, Nov 2026: no game or app uses the exact word. Echo-prefixed browser titles do exist, though: 'Echo Dash' (neon arcade) and 'Echo Loop Runner' (your delayed path becomes a damage field). So it must always be written as one word to stay distinctive and protectable. I picked it over 'Echoflick' because in a glowing logo the 'fli' in that name can read as a profanity. Store title: 'Echoveer: Neon Shadow Dodge' (27 chars).

candidates.name: Ghostlap
candidates.meaning: ghost + lap. Borrowed from the racing-game 'ghost lap', where a ghost replays your own earlier run. Here that ghost is hunting you.
candidates.rationale: Of all the candidates, this one matches the replay-shadow mechanic most closely, and players get it at once from racing games. It is still a new compound, so it suits a trademark. Short (8), two strong syllables, and the o in GHOST can become the glowing hexagon. No negative meanings in en/tr/de/it/fr/es. I chose it over 'lag' blends because 'lag' means latency, a negative in games, and Turkish 'lağım' means sewer. Web check: no game or app named Ghostlap. Store title: 'Ghostlap: Beat Your Shadow' (26).

candidates.name: Umbrisk
candidates.meaning: umbra (Latin: shadow) + brisk (quick, lively). A quick dash away from your own shadow.
candidates.rationale: A coined single word that suits a trademark, with a sporty, energetic sound (um-BRISK) that fits a reflex arcade game. Umbra is understood through the Romance-language shadow words (it. ombra, es. sombra, fr. ombre) without copying any of them. Its only existing use is as the Scandinavian word for 'Umbrian' (the old Italian language/region), which is harmless. No negatives in en/tr/de/it/fr/es. I avoided 'shade' blends because German 'schade' means 'what a pity' and English 'throw shade' means an insult. Store title: 'Umbrisk: Shadow Reflex' (22).

candidates.name: Ombrix
candidates.meaning: ombra (Italian: shadow) + the techy suffix -ix: 'the shadow device / shadow entity'.
candidates.rationale: A fully coined, very distinctive 6-letter mark, which is ideal for search and trademark. It sounds punchy and arcade-like in every target language (Turkish readers say it 'ombriks' naturally). The O can be the round glowing player, with an X-shaped laser cross as the ending. Web check: no exact match (a game character 'Professor Umbrix' exists, spelled differently and in another category). No negatives in en/tr/de/it/fr/es. Store title: 'Ombrix: Outrun Your Shadow' (26).

candidates.name: Pastpulse
candidates.meaning: past + pulse. Your own past movement pulses along behind you as a living shadow.
candidates.rationale: It describes the replay-delay mechanic exactly, and the P-P alliteration makes it easy to remember. A pulse is also a natural neon/glow animation for the logo. I deliberately used 'Past' rather than 'After-' blends (Afterself, Afterwisp, Afterglide), because German 'After' means anus, which breaks the no-negative-meaning rule for DE. No negatives in en/tr/de/it/fr/es. Web check: no game or app named Pastpulse. Store title: 'Pastpulse: Shadow Arcade' (24).

candidates.name: Glintail
candidates.meaning: glint (a spark of light) + tail. The bright spark is you; the tail is the shadow tailing you.
candidates.rationale: Short (8), gentle and friendly-sounding, which suits a 13+ casual audience. The name holds the whole game in two images: a glowing hero and a pursuer on its tail. The shared T in 'glint/tail' gives a neat visual blend, and the dot of the i can be a gold star pickup. No negatives in en/tr/de/it/fr/es. Web check: no game or app named Glintail. Store title: 'Glintail: Shadow Escape' (23).

candidates.name: Trailtwin
candidates.meaning: trail + twin. The twin that walks your own trail a few seconds behind you.
candidates.rationale: Plain English, but the compound is new and specific. The double T allows a mirrored logo (the second T as the dimmed teal shadow of the first, purple one), and 'twin' leads naturally into the 2-shadow stage. No negatives in en/tr/de/it/fr/es. Web check: no game called Trailtwin (only the unrelated 'Twin Trials' FPS on Steam, which is different enough). Store title: 'Trailtwin: Shadow Chase' (23).

candidates.name: Umbravoid
candidates.meaning: umbra (shadow) + avoid, with 'void' hidden inside, which points to the black hole maps.
candidates.rationale: A double pun: avoid your umbra, and the void (black hole) setting. Strong sci-fi neon tone that suits the late-game maps. Many games already use 'Umbra' on its own (UMBRA, Umbrafall, Umbra Survivors), so it must be used as one fused word, never 'Umbra Void', to stay distinctive. Web check: no exact match. No negatives in en/tr/de/it/fr/es ('void' here means space/emptiness). Store title: 'Umbravoid: Dodge Your Shadow' (28).

candidates.name: Phantrail
candidates.meaning: phantom + trail. A phantom that rides your trail.
candidates.rationale: Smoothly fused ('phantom' and 'trail' share the T sound). It feels mysterious and fast without being horror, which suits 13+. The 'ph' spelling makes it visually distinctive and easy to own in search. No negatives in en/tr/de/it/fr/es (es. fantasma, it. fantasma, fr. fantôme are all neutral). Web check: no game or app named Phantrail. Store title: 'Phantrail: Neon Shadow Run' (26).

candidates.name: Tracewisp
candidates.meaning: trace + wisp (as in will-o'-the-wisp). A wisp of light that leaves a trace, and that trace comes after you.
candidates.rationale: A soft, magical feel that suits the 'Magic Lumos' brand and the glowing geometric characters. The wordmark could draw the 'wisp' as a fading trail after the solid 'Trace'. No negatives in en/tr/de/it/fr/es. Web check: no game or app named Tracewisp. Store title: 'Tracewisp: Shadow Arcade' (24).
